name: Capsule Technologies
old_description: Philips Capsule is now part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio of solutions – a comprehensive, clinically focused ecosystem designed to enhance care delivery across the healthcare enterprise, with a goal of improving patient outcomes and reducing clinician burnout.
about:
Capsule Technologies, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, operates as part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio following its acquisition by Philips. The company focuses on healthcare informatics, providing a vendor-neutral platform that connects medical devices and clinical systems across hospital enterprises.

The company’s portfolio spans medical device integration, clinical surveillance, patient monitoring, virtual care, retrospective analytics, and clinical information systems. Its platform captures live-streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices — including measurements, settings, alarms, and waveforms — and delivers it using industry-standard protocols to more than 100 downstream systems such as electronic health records, clinical information systems, and alarm management tools. Key product lines include Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress, the Medical Device Information Platform, eCareManager, Clinical Insights Manager, Capsule Surveillance, and IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia (ICCA).

Capsule serves hospitals and health systems worldwide, with installations at organizations such as Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. Its solutions target acute care environments including intensive care units, perioperative settings, and general wards, aiming to reduce clinician burnout and improve patient outcomes through automated data capture and clinical decision support.

The company emphasizes its vendor-neutral, open ecosystem approach, which allows healthcare providers to leverage existing infrastructure while expanding capabilities incrementally. It also highlights deep clinical and operational experience, stating that its support extends beyond technology to fit workflows and enable clinical staff rather than burden them.
